title: Thioacetazone (historical, HIV-lethal)
dek: A cheap thiourea from the streptomycin era. Stevens–Johnson in people with HIV made it a “do not” more than a drug. HadC/HAD chemistry is a mycolate footnote, not a 2025 regimen letter.
story: Thioacetazone (thiacetazone) was an oral companion in older East African regimens. It is not in WHO 2024–2025 preferred lists. Severe cutaneous reactions, including Stevens–Johnson syndrome, cluster in people with HIV. That toxicity, not MIC poetry, retired it.

Mechanistically it intersects mycolate synthesis (HadABC dehydratase neighbourhood / related FAS-II steps — report cautiously, catalogues are thin). Cross-talk with ETH/INH pathways appears in old papers. None of that is a reason to reconstruct HRZ+thioacetazone because a freezer still has tablets.
If a genome pipeline still emits “thioacetazone R,” treat it as historical annotation. Do not let it alter BPaLM.
deepTitle: Why it still appears in BAMs
deep: Some mutation databases never deleted the rows.
Veterinary and very-old NTP documents still mention it. Date-stamp them.
SJS risk in HIV is the teaching point for why “cheap oral” is not enough.
Not the same molecule as ethionamide, despite the thio- prefix.
